newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH up sharply on DFS acquisition deal.
newsitem.headline: LVMH up sharply on DFS acquisition deal.

text.p: Shares in luxury goods group LVMH jumped on Wednesday after the company announced it had struck an agreement to acquire control of the San Francisco-based luxury goods distributor DFS for 12.6 billion francs to increase its presence in the Pacific rim.
The stock was up 3.59 percent at 1,155 francs at 0930 GMT, far outpacing the CAC-40 index's 0.41 percent advance.

"It's a very good deal," said one trader, referring to the importance of the fast-growing Asia-Pacific market for the group. But he had few details. Brokers said the company was hosting an analysts' meeting on Wednesday morning in the town of Cognac.
Another trader said his investment firm was waiting for more detail before considering a change in earnings forecasts or stock rating.
"This is unusual for them," the trader said, adding that the group had not previously turned to the retail sector. "Apparently, though, most people think it's good," he said.

LVMH said earlier in a statement that DFS was the world's largest luxury products distributor with annual sales of more than 15 billion francs, 180 boutiques and 20 years' experience in retailing in Asia.
"Thanks to this acquisition, LVMH will increase its presence in the Asia-Pacific region and emerging countries, a future growth area," it said.
The company said it would keep DFS's management team in place, and said the group would be managed independently of LVMH's other businesses.
It said in its statement that the acquisition agreement hinged on certain conditions but did not elaborate. Company officials were not immediately available for comment.

The New York Times reported on Wednesday that billionaire Robert Miller, who owns 38.75 percent of the DFS duty-free store empire, was trying to block a sale by his partners. It reported Miller said the deal would violate the terms of an agreement he signed in 1991 with his partners.
